title: Stride-based kernel-aware batching to reduce padding and align kernels
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: existing seqlen bucketing reduces padding but often mixes sequences that force suboptimal kernel choices and misalign with vectorized kernels, increasing tail latency and GPU cycles. This PR introduces a stride-based batching heuristic that groups in-flight requests into stride windows (e.g. 1-8,9-16,17-32 tokens) but additionally factors in kernel alignment preferences and a lightweight padding cost estimator so that batches prefer sequence lengths that map to the same high-throughput kernel path. Implementation summary: 1) New stride-batcher module that computes a sequence-length stride index and maintains per-stride pending queues with time-aware draining thresholds; 2) Kernel selector integration: each stride tracks preferred kernel variants (fp16/qat/quant) and we only co-batch requests when preferred-kernel overlap >= threshold to avoid kernel-switch stalls; 3) Padding estimator: online estimator predicts effective extra tokens added by padding per candidate batch and the scheduler uses a cost function (latency + token-cost) to decide whether to wait or dispatch now; 4) KV-cache interaction: improved cache lifetime alignment ensures requests with hot KV keys are prioritized to the same batch when safe and TTL boundaries are respected to avoid stale cache reads; 5) Continuous-batching compatibility: the stride-batcher hooks into existing continuous batching loop with backpressure signals to keep p95 SLOs. Performance: microbenchmarks on c5-gpu-4 (A100-equivalent) show 9-16% reduction in effective padded tokens per batch and 8-14% p95 latency reduction for chat workloads with highly skewed seq-len distributions; overall cost-per-token reduced by ~12% in our internal synthetic workloads. Rollout plan: staged feature flag behind 'stride_batcher' with canary traffic at 10% -> 30% -> 100% with automatic rollback if p95 increases >5% or token-cost increases >6%. Migration notes: no model re-training required; clients unaffected, API unchanged. Known limitations: very short-lived bursts (<10ms inter-arrival) may not benefit and can add scheduling overhead; kernel-preference thresholds require periodic calibration per hardware family. Related tickets: ENG-5123 evaluation harness additions and ENG-5189 kernel selector refactor.
